waist_cut.note: Not re-tuned. Reported so the cut can be checked against the rig it is applied to, exactly as for Maestro.

bone_diff.prefix: mixamorig: (as Fiamma, unlike Maestro's bare names)
bone_diff.note: Colosso's rig is the Fiamma rig shape: 28 joints, `mixamorig:` prefix, spine chain ascending (Spine -> Spine1 -> Spine2), and both Toe_End joints present. Every one of the 14 bones in BONE_REGION was found in skins[0].joints by name; nothing is missing and nothing is invented. Against Maestro the differences are the prefix, the spine numbering direction and the two Toe_End joints - all three of which change no triangle, because Maestro's map covers the same anatomy.

neutral_breakdown.note: the mask is a permission map: these are the texels it covers that the shader cannot recolour at all, because sat_min rejects the greys and the value window rejects the near-black and the blown-out

skin_anchor.measured_on: strict protected-group triangles (head, arms, forearms, hands, shins)

inmask_skin_tone_attribution.rule: one owner per triangle - the BONE_REGION bone dominating the most of that triangle's three vertices, ties broken by bone name - so the per-bone rows are a partition and sum to the texel count they explain
inmask_skin_tone_attribution.unattributed_note: texels inside the mask that no garment-bone triangle owns: protected geometry caught by the 1.2 px edge soften, or coverage overlap between islands

strict_all_three_vertices_secondary.note: the strict rule draws a triangle only when all three vertices are dominated by the same bone, so a texel on a mixed-dominance triangle belongs to no bone and is missing here; this is why the strict rows never summed to the total and must not be read as a partition

shader_family_weight_mirror.formula: w = (1 - smoothstep(hue_tol_deg*0.55, hue_tol_deg, dh)) * ss((s - sat_min)/0.12) * ss((v - val_min)/0.12), value gate off - outfit_region_recolour.gdshader::family_weight, run with the MASK_DEFAULTS windows and the anchors' modal hues
shader_family_weight_mirror.note: the skin of this athlete sits at the centre of both anchors' ramps, so the shader recolours it at full weight for both families; outside the mask the mask is what keeps it out, and inside the mask nothing does

value_gate.split_defined_as: the boundary of the largest step of the 0.05-binned in-mask value histogram, near-empty low bins floored out

best_value_cut_for_skin_vs_garment_insid.note: skin side = the in-mask texels carrying the measured skin tone; garment side = the in-mask chromatic texels that are not skin-toned. This is the pair the shader has to decide on, and it does not separate.
best_value_cut_for_skin_vs_garment_insid.sampling: every second texel (step 2), the sample this whole block uses

best_value_cut_for_skin_vs_garment_measu.note: same scan against the whole measured skin population on the protected bones (outside the mask), against the same garment mass inside it.
best_value_cut_for_skin_vs_garment_measu.sampling: every second texel (step 2), the sample this whole block uses

value_gate.note: The split at 0.50 is the boundary of the largest step of the 0.05-binned in-mask value histogram (0.45-0.50 -> 0.50-0.55, x1.635); the second largest is x1.588 one bin higher. It is NOT the density discontinuity Maestro's split sits on (x5.34): at 0.01 resolution the histogram is still rising through the split (x1.101), and the largest 1%-bin step in the transition is x1.850 at 0.55->0.56, inside the light family's own peak. What no value cut fixes is what it separates: the light side is the character's own skin.
value_gate.skin_population_texels_below_the_split_n: population = on-skin texels with s >= sat_min (the same gate as skin_toned_texels_in_the_light_side); the report used to carry the ungated count of every on-skin texel below the split, which is a different population and 3.7x larger

skin_protection.skin_recolourable_verdict: NO. The skin population measured on the protected bones sits at hue 24.0 deg - inside the garment's own hue band (21-45 deg) - so the shader's 45 deg family test cannot reject it: 64.5% of the skin texels answer to the leather anchor and 64.5% to the light anchor. Inside the mask, 45059 sampled texels (12.67% of it) carry that exact skin tone, on bare skin the garment bones own: mixamorig:RightUpLeg 19189, mixamorig:LeftShoulder 12983, mixamorig:RightShoulder 11544, mixamorig:Spine 632. A value gate separates the dark leather from the light family, but the light family IS the skin: 44077 of those 45059 texels (97.8%) sit above the split. Pushed as far as it goes, the best single value cut inside the mask (0.54) still puts 21860 chromatic garment texels on the skin's side and 5909 skin-toned texels on the garment's side, balanced accuracy 0.848 - below the 0.95 a separation would need.

verdict: MASK USABLE AS A PERMISSION MAP, NOT USABLE AS A TWO-FAMILY RECOLOUR MAP. The mask itself is sound: 2766 torso / 1583 hip / 947 foot triangles, 1421477 covered texels (0.3389 of the atlas), strict leak on the head, hands, forearms, arms and shins at or below 0.0001 of each group's own UV area. It is NOT sufficient to keep Colosso's skin out of a recolour: the atlas's whole chromatic content lives in hue 21-45 deg, the anchors are 6.0 deg apart under a 45.0 deg tolerance, so the hue test separates nothing (1048218 of 1421791 masked texels answer to both anchors, including every skin-toned texel inside the mask). The value test splits the dark mass from the light one at 0.50 (x1.635 in 0.05 bins against Maestro's x5.34, i.e. a ramp, not a discontinuity), but what it cannot separate is what the split puts on the light side: 44077 of the 45059 skin-toned sampled texels inside the mask (97.8%) are above it, and the best single value cut for skin-vs-garment inside the mask still lands 21860 chromatic garment texels on the skin's side. 45059 sampled masked texels (12.67% of the mask) carry the character's own skin tone, and 51.48% of the mask is chromatic and inside the shader's value window at all.
